author: Japanese Research Division, Military History Section, Headquarters, Army Forces Far East / U.S. Army Forces Far East
title: Japanese Monographs
publisher: Military History Section, Headquarters, Army Forces Far East, Tokyo
edition: Series of about 187 numbered monographs prepared 1946–1960; cite the individual monograph by number and title in the citation note
notes: The Japanese-side operational record that is actually in English, and the reason this arc need not be written entirely out of American sources. On instructions issued 12 October 1945, former Japanese officers who had held the relevant command and staff appointments wrote up their operations under the supervision of the Demobilization Bureaux; the drafts were translated and rewritten in English by the Japanese Research Division. The series covers what the packs need — Philippines Operations Record (Mono 1), Midway Operations (Mono 93), Okinawa Operations Record (Mono 135), and the Southeast Area and submarine records for the Solomons. Read the series' own warning first, and pass it on in every note that cites one. The introduction says most original orders, plans and unit journals were lost or destroyed, that many important orders, plans and estimates 'have been reconstructed from memory and therefore are not textually identical with the originals', and that they are nevertheless 'believed to be generally accurate and reliable'. That is a document reconstructed from memory by the losing side under the occupying army: cite a monograph for what a Japanese commander said he intended, in the manner of a memoir, and never for the wording of an order. This registry holds the series as one entry, as it does source:byu-wwi-archive; a monograph a pack comes to lean on heavily earns its own entry then.
